gap_statement: Cross-stage contestability across making and evaluation lacks direct empirical characterisation.
why_gap_matters: Final-output evaluations cannot locate where a future becomes difficult to challenge.
insight: Contestability may be preserved or lost at more than one transformation in the research trajectory.
contribution_statement: A sequential mixed-method empirical account of how making affordances and evaluation protocols shape contestability across three micro-speculations.
required_evidence_type: Completed human Study A and Study B data linked through artefact traces; blinded coding; uncertainty; construct checks.
limitation: No formal human sessions have been run; the apparatus and synthetic pipeline are not outcome evidence.
boundary_language: Applies only to the implemented tasks, samples, conditions, and measures.
reviewer_defense_note: Do not promote the headline hypothesis until human results and falsification checks are frozen.

gap_statement: Closed correctness-oriented rubrics may measure a different construct from interpretive openness in speculative artefacts.
why_gap_matters: A reliable rubric can still be construct-invalid for the intended speculative knowledge goal.
insight: The evaluation protocol is itself an interaction that can orient subsequent interpretation.
contribution_statement: A controlled comparison of closed defect/compliance and ambiguity-preserving protocols followed by an identical neutral probe.
required_evidence_type: Powered human audience comparison; common-probe coding; comprehension and verbosity diagnostics.
limitation: Final sample size and model family require pilot dispersion and clustering estimates.
boundary_language: No claim that open protocols are universally superior or that every ambiguity is valuable.
reviewer_defense_note: Primary outcome comes from the common probe rather than treatment-specific questions.

gap_statement: A controlled and auditable apparatus is needed to manipulate revision locality without provider randomness.
why_gap_matters: Uncontrolled model variation can be mistaken for an interface effect.
insight: Fixed pre-generated candidates can isolate representational affordance for a scoped mechanism study.
contribution_statement: A local-first apparatus with counterbalancing, common undo controls, a semantically addressable local condition, immutable returns, blinding, and evidence-boundary gates.
required_evidence_type: Deterministic tests; browser smoke evidence; non-local request audit; synthetic end-to-end pipeline.
limitation: The fixed simulator is less ecologically valid than a live generative provider.
boundary_language: The apparatus establishes controlled feasibility, not human benefit or speculative quality.
reviewer_defense_note: Provider-free standardisation is disclosed and treated as a scope condition.

gap_statement: Technical integrity, provenance, audience interpretation, and curatorial retention are often collapsed or treated as substitutable.
why_gap_matters: A single quality score can hide technically valid but interpretively closed or curatorially rejected artefacts.
insight: Warrant conflicts should be analysed as linked cases rather than averaged.
contribution_statement: A trace-linked analysis of technical PASS, provenance, maker contestation, audience interpretation, and expert KEEP/REVISE/REJECT.
required_evidence_type: Completed human traces; deterministic technical audit; blinded expert decisions; audience interpretations; qualitative conflict analysis.
limitation: The internal five-class vocabulary has not been validated as a universal taxonomy.
boundary_language: Reports situated conflict patterns only; no universal warrant set or composite score.
reviewer_defense_note: Inductive coding precedes use of PACT classes as a sensitising lens.
